title: VIGIL run record
description: One audit run, reduced to VIGIL's own vocabulary. THE PRIVACY GUARANTEE IS STRUCTURAL: every string is an enum or a bounded pattern and additionalProperties is false at every level, so a path, repo name, hostname or finding description is unrepresentable rather than redacted. Adding a free-text field removes that guarantee, which is why L25 refuses one. REVISED 2026-07-31 against the first real run record: the original was written without ever having seen one and rejected it on 100+ counts, none of which were privacy violations. Where the disagreement was arbitrary, the observed shape wins — a schema is a description of what runs produce, and a gratuitous structural preference is what made version 1 reject everything.

vigil_version.description: 'unversioned' is permitted and is itself a signal: the skill could not self-identify, so any cross-version comparison of this record is unsound.

timestamp_bucket.description: Quarter granularity. Coarse enough not to fingerprint a session, fine enough to detect version drift across a corpus.

stack.description: Detected ecosystems and frameworks. A bounded enum, not a dependency list — 'fastapi' is a fact about a class of project, '@acme/billing-sdk' is a fact about a company.

tree_state.description: WHICH TREE THIS RECORD IS ABOUT. lessons/0010: a finding is relative to a tree, and nothing forces you to say which one. The same repository gives different correct answers depending on whether you scan the working tree, the tracked tree or history — one real audit measured 32 / 0 / 1 secrets across the three. A record that does not say cannot be aggregated with one that does, so like `shared` this has no default and privacy_gate refuses to bundle a record lacking it. Not required in the record: a run may legitimately not know, and a record that admits ignorance is better than one that guesses.

missing.description: Aggregated across a corpus, this is the preflight gap report.

verdict.description: scored = a probe ran and produced evidence. na = not applicable, and must cite a trigger. ne = NO EVIDENCE: applicable, but nothing could evidence it either way.

ceiling.description: THE D1 SIGNAL. The evidence ceiling this cluster could reach. A ceiling below 100 means no cluster-specific probe exists, so the score is bounded by what could not be checked. Aggregated across real runs this answers D1 empirically. null when the cluster did not score.

false_positives_withdrawn.description: Findings the auditor produced and then retracted before reporting. A rising count across a corpus means the rules are noisy upstream of the human.

shared.description: THE CONSENT RECORD. Deliberately has no default and is not required here: a record that was never asked cannot answer, and privacy_gate.py refuses to bundle any record lacking 'asked-accepted'. Consent is therefore structural — silence is unshareable by construction rather than by policy.

outcomes.description: THE LEARNING SIGNAL. What the human did with each finding — the only field carrying a judgement about VIGIL rather than about the run.

clusterPrefix.description: The cluster prefixes exactly as RULES.md Rule 6 defines them. NOT the finding-ID form: 'VIGIL-SEC-001' is an ID, 'SEC' is the prefix. Version 1 of this schema demanded 'VIGIL-SEC' and so contradicted RULES.md; L29 now cross-validates this list against it.
